notes: The Greek word can mean a full brother, a half-brother or a relative. The lists of names and the women at the cross are what the argument turns on.
Paul opposes Peter to his face in Antioch, and James seems to give the final word at the council of Jerusalem. Catholics and others read these differently.

The apostles write to slaves and to masters in a world where slavery was normal. They do not call for its abolition, and they say that in Christ master and slave are brothers. Philemon is the clearest case.
Paul greets women as co-workers and a deacon (Phoebe), and in other places asks women to be silent in the assembly. Mary Magdalene is the first to see the risen Lord.
The Bible does not describe the gesture. These are the passages about the name of the Trinity, and about a mark placed on the faithful.
